title: Ensure 'Maximum password age' is set to '365 or fewer days, but not 0'
profile_applicability:
•  Level 1 - Domain Controller
•  Level 1 - Member Server

branching.result_aggregation: PASS if the active branch verify step passes; SKIP if a branch is not applicable to this host (the other role); FAIL if the active branch check fails; ERROR if role detection fails or DomainRole value is unrecognised. Use the DC verify status for cis_result when is_dc is true; use the Member Server verify status when is_member is true.

objective: Audit CIS checkpoint 1.1.2: Ensure 'Maximum password age' is set to '{{ max_password_age_days }} or fewer days, but not 0'

playbook_input.description: Parameters the caller provides before execution

parameters.name: max_password_age_days
parameters.description: Maximum allowed password age in days (must be > 0 and ≤ this value)

fields.name: password_age_days
fields.description: Actual maximum password age in days as detected on the target host

steps.name: Check if the Windows server role is Domain Controller or Member Server
steps.function: 1. Check if the Windows server role is Domain Controller or Member Server using command: `(Get-WmiObject Win32_ComputerSystem).DomainRole`. Expected result: 4 or 5 for DC, 0-3 for Member Server.

steps.name: Check if Active Directory module is available for DC path
steps.function: 2. Check if Active Directory module is available for DC path using command: `Get-Module -ListAvailable -Name ActiveDirectory`. Expected result: module present.

steps.name: Check DC default domain password policy MaxPasswordAge
steps.function: 3. Check DC default domain password policy MaxPasswordAge using command: `(Get-ADDefaultDomainPasswordPolicy).MaxPasswordAge`. Expected result: days ≤ {{ max_password_age_days }} and > 0.

steps.name: Check DC GPO setting for Maximum password age
steps.function: 4. Check DC GPO setting for Maximum password age using command: `Get-GPO -Name "Default Domain Policy" | Get-GPOReport -ReportType Xml | Select-String 'MaxPasswordAge'`. Expected result: value ≤ {{ max_password_age_days }} and > 0.

steps.name: Check member server effective local policy Maximum password age
steps.function: 5. Check member server effective local policy Maximum password age using command: `$tmp = "$env:TEMP\secpol.cfg"; secedit /export /cfg $tmp /areas SECURITYPOLICY /quiet; Get-Content $tmp | Select-String 'MaximumPasswordAge'`. Expected result: value ≤ {{ max_password_age_days }} and > 0.

steps.name: Check if the policy value is not 0 for DC path
steps.function: 6. Check if the policy value is not 0 for DC path using command: `(Get-ADDefaultDomainPasswordPolicy).MaxPasswordAge`. Expected result: value > 0.

steps.name: Check if the policy value is not 0 for member server path
steps.function: 7. Check if the policy value is not 0 for member server path using command: `$tmp = "$env:TEMP\secpol.cfg"; secedit /export /cfg $tmp /areas SECURITYPOLICY /quiet; Get-Content $tmp | Select-String 'MaximumPasswordAge'`. Expected result: value > 0.

steps.name: Check if the policy value is {{ max_password_age_days }} or fewer days for DC path
steps.function: 8. Check if the policy value is {{ max_password_age_days }} or fewer days for DC path using command: `(Get-ADDefaultDomainPasswordPolicy).MaxPasswordAge`. Expected result: value ≤ {{ max_password_age_days }}.

steps.name: Check if the policy value is {{ max_password_age_days }} or fewer days for member server path
steps.function: 9. Check if the policy value is {{ max_password_age_days }} or fewer days for member server path using command: `$tmp = "$env:TEMP\secpol.cfg"; secedit /export /cfg $tmp /areas SECURITYPOLICY /quiet; Get-Content $tmp | Select-String 'MaximumPasswordAge'`. Expected result: value ≤ {{ max_password_age_days }}.

steps.name: Check if the policy is applied via Default Domain Policy GPO for DC
steps.function: 10. Check if the policy is applied via Default Domain Policy GPO for DC using command: `Get-GPO -Name "Default Domain Policy" | Get-GPOReport -ReportType Xml | Select-String 'MaxPasswordAge'`. Expected result: setting present.

steps.name: Check if the policy is applied via local security policy for member server
steps.function: 11. Check if the policy is applied via local security policy for member server using command: `$tmp = "$env:TEMP\secpol.cfg"; secedit /export /cfg $tmp /areas SECURITYPOLICY /quiet; Get-Content $tmp | Select-String 'MaximumPasswordAge'`. Expected result: setting present.

steps.name: Check if the OS is Windows for applicability
steps.function: 12. Check if the OS is Windows for applicability using command: `$env:OS`. Expected result: Windows_NT.

steps.name: Check if the domain controller role is valid for DC path
steps.function: 13. Check if the domain controller role is valid for DC path using command: `(Get-WmiObject Win32_ComputerSystem).DomainRole`. Expected result: 4 or 5.

steps.name: Check if the member server role is valid for member server path
steps.function: 14. Check if the member server role is valid for member server path using command: `(Get-WmiObject Win32_ComputerSystem).DomainRole`. Expected result: 0, 1, 2, or 3.

steps.name: Check if the password policy is globally effective for DC
steps.function: 15. Check if the password policy is globally effective for DC using command: `Get-ADDefaultDomainPasswordPolicy`. Expected result: policy object exists.

steps.name: Check if the password policy is locally effective for member server
steps.function: 16. Check if the password policy is locally effective for member server using command: `$tmp = "$env:TEMP\secpol.cfg"; secedit /export /cfg $tmp /areas SECURITYPOLICY /quiet; Get-Content $tmp | Select-String 'MaximumPasswordAge'`. Expected result: policy value present.

steps.name: Check if the policy value is within range 1-{{ max_password_age_days }} for DC
steps.function: 17. Check if the policy value is within range 1-{{ max_password_age_days }} for DC using command: `(Get-ADDefaultDomainPasswordPolicy).MaxPasswordAge`. Expected result: value between 1 and {{ max_password_age_days }}.

steps.name: Check if the policy value is within range 1-{{ max_password_age_days }} for member server
steps.function: 18. Check if the policy value is within range 1-{{ max_password_age_days }} for member server using command: `$tmp = "$env:TEMP\secpol.cfg"; secedit /export /cfg $tmp /areas SECURITYPOLICY /quiet; Get-Content $tmp | Select-String 'MaximumPasswordAge'`. Expected result: value between 1 and {{ max_password_age_days }}.

steps.name: Check if the policy is configured in Default Domain Policy GPO for DC
steps.function: 19. Check if the policy is configured in Default Domain Policy GPO for DC using command: `Get-GPO -Name "Default Domain Policy" | Get-GPOReport -ReportType Xml | Select-String 'MaxPasswordAge'`. Expected result: setting exists.

compliance_constraints: This checkpoint applies to BOTH Domain Controllers (DomainRole 4/5) AND Member Servers (DomainRole 1-3). Detect the server role first using (Get-WmiObject Win32_ComputerSystem).DomainRole, then audit via the correct path: DC → Active Directory / GPO cmdlets; Member Server → secedit /export /areas SECURITYPOLICY. Do NOT return SKIP for a Member Server — it is a valid audit target.
Use failed_when: false on all audit tasks (except set_fact, debug) so all checks complete and report status
If the audit targets a specific software/service (e.g., GDM, GNOME, sshd, httpd), FIRST check if it is installed. If NOT installed, report SKIP for all checks.
This is an AUDIT playbook — it MUST NOT make any changes to the system. All tasks must be read-only (shell commands, stat, slurp, command with check-only flags, etc.).
The maximum password age threshold is configurable via the input parameter max_password_age_days (default 180). All comparisons must use this parameter instead of a hardcoded 365.
reference_procedure: Navigate to the UI Path articulated in the Remediation section and confirm it is set as prescribed.
